The median building in West Lawn dates to 1954, and 82.3 percent of its 9,758 housing units were up before 1970. 20.8 percent are prewar. The community-area figures bucket at 1970 rather than 1978, so treat 82.3 percent as a floor on the pre-1978 share here, not a ceiling.

Count it by household and West Lawn is 7,225 owning against 2,262 renting, 76.2 percent owner occupied. Count it by building and it is 70.2 percent detached, 2.2 percent attached, 26.9 percent in twos or more. Median unit: 6.1 rooms. Median home value is $259,593.

Set against the other places covered here, West Lawn is furthest from the middle on three things: townhomes and rowhouses at 2.2 percent against a 7.5 percent average, housing built before 1970 at 82.3 percent against a 56.9 percent average and prewar housing at 20.8 percent against a 15.8 percent average.

Source: Chicago Metropolitan Agency for Planning, Community Data Snapshots 2026, drawing on American Community Survey 2024 estimates. Every dollar figure on this page is a published Census estimate of what homes in the area are worth. None of it is a price for work.

How the age of the stock changes the work here

A 1954 median build year means plaster as well as drywall, and the two do not take a repair the same way. Plaster cracks along the lath and comes back if it is only filled, so the honest version of a wall repair here is longer than a drywall patch and should read that way on the quote. With 6.1 rooms on the median unit, the trim is the other half of the job. The 7,225 to 2,262 split between owning and renting in West Lawn means the same street can want two different things. A contractor who prices both the same way is wrong about one of them.

The lines a quote for West Lawn needs to show

  • Distance, stated. West Lawn is 4.7 straight-line miles from the shop. Travel to West Lawn is not a hidden line item on this site and it should not be one on a written quote either.
  • Containment, not just paint. 82.3 percent of housing in West Lawn was built before 1970, so on most addresses here the lead-safe setup and the cleanup are part of the job and part of the hours.
  • Plaster as well as drywall. 20.8 percent of West Lawn is prewar. Plaster cracks along the lath and comes back if it is only filled, so wall repair is a different line from wall painting.
  • Trim, counted separately. At a median of 6.1 rooms, casing, baseboard and doors are the half of an interior that actually varies. A single number for the whole house hides it.

What the housing here is likely made of

Most of it is brick bungalow, Cape Cod and early ranch. The walls are masonry, so exterior paint concentrates in trim, soffit, fascia, garage surround and doors. West Lawn interiors are trim-heavy for their square footage.

It is read off exactly two things: the 1954 median build year, and the split between 70.2 percent detached houses, 2.2 percent attached homes and 26.9 percent in buildings of two units or more.

Inference, and worth saying so. Wall material in West Lawn is not in the Census tables or the regional data, which is why that sentence carries no number when everything else here does.

Next door is not the same job

West Lawn and Chicago Lawn are 1.3 miles apart and are quoted differently, which is the whole argument for reading a page about your own town rather than a page about the region. They part company on detached-house share (70.2 percent against 44.6 percent); share of units in buildings of two or more (26.9 percent against 52.9 percent); prewar share (20.8 percent against 38.6 percent).

Lead-safe work on West Lawn houses

The community-area tables stop at 1970 and never draw a 1978 line. What they give is 82.3 percent built before 1970, which is a floor rather than an answer, and no source puts a number on the gap for West Lawn. Anything built before 1978 sits inside the federal Renovation, Repair and Painting rule the moment work disturbs its paint. Illinois never took the program on, so the agency behind it here is EPA itself.

Read it as a method rather than a prohibition. Below roughly six square feet of disturbed paint in a room, or twenty outside, it does not bite. Above that, and on any window replacement in West Lawn at all, it decides how the room is sealed and how it is left. On 6.1-room housing that threshold arrives early.

None of it is graded at the town line. The rule attaches to a build year and to the work being done, so the number worth checking is the one on your own deed in West Lawn.

None of that is a reason to leave a West Lawn house unpainted. It is a reason to know what the setup looks like before anyone opens a sander, and to hear it from the person doing the work rather than from a website.

No lead-safe certification is claimed anywhere on this site, because no number has been provided to put here. The panel below leaves the slot open on purpose, in West Lawn and everywhere else. Ask any contractor for theirs.

Coverage and scheduling for West Lawn

It is 4.7 straight-line miles between 7900 W. 83rd St. in Bridgeview and West Lawn. Southwest of the Loop is the half of Chicago this shop treats as normal working distance, and the housing on that side goes up the same way the inner suburbs did.

For scale, the nearest other place on this site is Chicago Lawn, 1.3 miles from West Lawn, and West Lawn sits in Cook County.

What will not be pretended here is coverage of the whole city. Chicago is enormous and heavily contested, and a north side call is better served by somebody on the north side. Ask, and you will be told which one you are before anything gets scheduled.

Questions

Asked about West Lawn

Can it be done a room at a time?

It can. Splitting a 6.1-room house into phases is normal and it is priced as phases rather than as a discount on the whole. The trade-off is setup time, because masking and protecting a room costs the same whether it is one room or the fourth.

What changes the price most on a house here?

Prep. Housing here runs to a 1954 median, which means several coats are already on the woodwork and some of them were put on badly. Undoing that is the expensive part, and it is the part that a fast number leaves out and a slow one explains.

Why do these figures cover the community area rather than my ZIP code?

Because ZIP codes cut through neighborhood lines and community areas do not. One ZIP on the southwest side covers three different neighborhoods with three different kinds of housing, so a page built on it would be describing an average of places that have nothing to do with each other. The 9,758 housing units counted here are the ones inside West Lawn, and the source is named at the bottom of the page.

My house in West Lawn is plaster, not drywall. Is that a problem?

It is not a problem, it is a different repair. Plaster cracks along the lath and comes back if it is only filled, so the fix has to address the movement rather than the line. With a 1954 median build year most of West Lawn is plaster over lath on at least some walls and ceilings. Say so when you call, because it changes the time estimate and it is better said before the quote than after.
